fields.problem:
Title: Equivalence of Definitions of Real Natural Logarithm/Proof 1

{{TFAE|def = Real Natural Logarithm}}

=== [[Definition:Natural Logarithm/Positive Real/Definition 1|Definition 1]] ===
The '''[[Definition:Real Natural Logarithm|(natural) logarithm]]''' of $x$ is the [[Definition:Real-Valued Function|real-valued function]] defined on $\R_{>0}$ as:
:$\ds \forall x \in \R_{>0}: \ln x := \int_1^x \frac {\d t} t$
=== [[Definition:Natural Logarithm/Positive Real/Definition 2|Definition 2]] ===
Let $x \in \R$ be a [[Definition:Real Number|real number]] such that $x > 0$.

The '''[[Definition:Real Natural Logarithm|(natural) logarithm]]''' of $x$ is defined as:

:$\ln x := y \in \R: e^y = x$

where $e$ is [[Definition:Euler's Number|Euler's number]].
=== [[Definition:Natural Logarithm/Positive Real/Definition 3|Definition 3]] ===
Let $x \in \R$ be a [[Definition:Real Number|real number]] such that $x > 0$.

The '''[[Definition:Real Natural Logarithm|(natural) logarithm]]''' of $x$ is defined as:

:$\ds \ln x := \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} n \paren {\sqrt [n] x - 1}$
fields.witness: Take x=1 over the reals. The defining integral has identical endpoints: F(1)=∫₁¹(1/t)dt=0. The claimed value is e¹=e, which is strictly positive and hence nonzero.
